headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading error: Dify can ingest and act on Dagster outputs, while Dagster has no isolation or write surface to constrain the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, filesystem read/write, MCP, or stdin/stdout surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Dify output by default. Dify can wire tools into agent/workflow flows, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel. The only plausible bridge is unusual manual copy-paste or external orchestration, so injection risk is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Dify-generated text into a Dagster config or prompt field
IF an external shared channel is added between Dify and Dagster
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste between systems during reviews
Require provenance labels on any text moved from Dify to Dagster
Use separate workspaces for orchestration text and pipeline code
Add a short human review step before any pasted instructions are executed

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no network egress, but Dify handles knowledge base content, conversation logs, model-provider API keys, and tool credentials. Because Dify can expose uploaded files to its agent/workflow tools, any shared workspace or copied content can leak into outputs. The pairwise path is plausible in default Dify deployments, though Dagster itself is not a direct exfiltrator.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs are copied into Dify knowledge-base files or conversation logs
IF Dify tools are configured to return uploaded file contents in responses
mitigations: Keep Dagster artifacts out of Dify knowledge bases
Redact secrets before any upload to Dify
Restrict Dify tool outputs to summaries instead of raw files
Separate credentials used by Dify from any Dagster-managed data

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files or modify git state, but Dify can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write files in its server-side code tool. That creates overlapping mutation risk on shared resources if both are pointed at the same workspace or datastore. The conflict is not proven by default, but Dify's broader write surface makes coordination failures plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory or datastore
IF Dify code tools are allowed to mutate files that Dagster also reads
mitigations: Assign separate directories for Dagster and Dify outputs
Disable Dify write actions for shared resources
Add file-locking or queueing around any shared datastore
Review any workflow that lets Dify mutate pipeline code

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can treat tool outputs as agent/workflow inputs, and Dagster can produce pipeline metadata or transformed data that Dify may render or act on. If Dify trusts Dagster output without verification, a bad pipeline result can cascade into downstream actions or user-facing answers. Because Dify has tool execution authority, the blast radius can extend beyond a single response.
conditions: IF Dify uses Dagster-produced values as authoritative tool inputs
IF no validation step checks Dagster outputs before Dify acts on them
mitigations: Add schema validation for Dagster outputs before Dify consumes them
Require human approval for any Dify action based on pipeline results
Log and diff Dagster outputs before downstream use
Limit Dify tools to read-only actions for pipeline-derived data

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster is open-source and shows no touched data classes, while Dify explicitly handles knowledge base content, conversation logs, model-provider API keys, and tool credentials. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated data is placed into Dify without matching retention or residency controls. The other agent is not cited for residency because its profile does not specify one.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Dify conversation logs or knowledge-base files
IF Dify retention or residency settings differ from the governing policy
mitigations: Block regulated data from Dify unless policy is confirmed
Set explicit retention limits for conversation logs
Document where knowledge-base files are stored
Review secret-handling settings before enabling production use
